claude.rationale: The deal is a reverse-triangular merger in which Merger Sub merges into PharMerica, leaving PharMerica intact as the surviving legal entity wholly owned by Parent, "with no carve-out, spin-off, or separation of the customer-facing pharmacy business from its operating entity disclosed." Because the customer-facing pharmacy product (T4) and operating processes (T5) remain within a single surviving entity that transfers whole, product and process move together — gap_45=0. Likewise the proxy "identifies no separation of the customer-facing pharmacy product or operating processes from the surviving legal entity," and executives/awards continue under existing schedules, so processes and the organization/people (T6) stay coherently together — gap_56=0. Ownership control shifts from public shareholders to a KKR-affiliated holding company (with minority WBA interest), coding T1 as replace.

gemini.rationale: The transaction was structured as a reverse-triangular merger where PharMerica survived intact as a wholly owned subsidiary of a new KKR-affiliated holding company. The proxy statement identifies no separation of the customer-facing pharmacy product (T4) or operating processes (T5) from the surviving legal entity, nor any separation of the organization (T6). Therefore, there are no structural gaps between T4/T5 or T5/T6 at closing.

Because T4 product and T5 processes crossed together inside the unbroken surviving entity, gap_45 is 0; likewise T5 processes and T6 organization remained inside that same intact entity with no documented process-without-people split at closing, so gap_56 is 0.
